newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr steady as RBA holds rates.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr steady as RBA holds rates.

text.p: The Australian dollar held steady atop 79 cents after the Reserve Bank left official rates unchanged at its morning money market operation.

There had been concerns the central bank would cut its 7.00 percent official cash rate following the monthly meeting of its policy-making board on Tuesday, although analysts had been reasonably confident it would hold off for the moment.

They thought the inaction meant the market could probably relax until the next RBA board meeting on October 1 which should support the dollar in the interim. By 9.35 am (2335 GMT) it was holding at US$0.7913/18, unchanged from Tuesday's finish.
It was just as quiet on the crosses at 86.36/46 yen from 86.48/58 late Tuesday and 1.1745/57 marks from 1.1757/69.
Dealers were somewhat surprised the currency had not made more of the opportunity which suggested it could be vulnerable.

"It looks like the market got a little long in anticipation of no change and now everyone is waiting for a bounce to sell into," said one. "The offshore guys should be relieved, and may take it up later, but for the moment its an anti-climax."
There were no domestic economic data to provide a lead, either, so a US$0.7895/7925 range looked likely for the near term.
